Render one frame of a scene

Source: R/interop.R
scene_frame.Rd

scene_frame() renders the frame shown at time t (in seconds) of a scene, without writing a video: plays that end before t step through their frames without drawing them (so updaters reach the state a render gives), and the play running at t is drawn at its last frame at or before t, the frame a video shows then. It is a quick way to look at any point of a scene while writing it; plot() shows the frame. t = Inf gives the last frame.

Usage

scene_frame(scene, t = Inf, quality = "l", ...)

expect_snapshot_frame(scene, t = Inf, name = "frame", quality = "l", ...)

Arguments

scene

A Scene class, a construct function or a scene object, as render() takes.

t

Time in seconds.

quality

Quality flag or preset name.

...

Further manim_config() settings.

name

Snapshot name for expect_snapshot_frame().

Value

scene_frame() returns a manim_frame_image, a native raster.

Details

expect_snapshot_frame() is a testthat expectation for packages that make scenes: it saves the frame as a PNG snapshot (see testthat::expect_snapshot_file()) and fails when it changes.

Examples

f <- scene_frame(function(self) self$play(Create(Circle()), run_time = 2), t = 1)
plot(f)
